title: the WSG climbing - Table 15 (the climbing movement rates)
audit_comment: The climbing slice pins Table 15 (the 13 surface rows x the three condition rates in feet per round for a thief with the per-cell thief-or-mountaineering restrictions), the climbing prose (the half rate, the dex adjustment, the no-tools assumption), the encumbrance modifications, the surface types and conditions and the chance-of-falling rating (rules/wsgclimb.h, prefix wcs); census 359 -> 360.

banner.title: The WSG CLIMBING, R435: Table 15 (the climbing movement rates - the 13 surface rows x the non-slippery, slightly slippery and slippery feet-per-round rates for a thief, with the asterisked cells climbable only by a thief or a mountaineering-proficient character using special tools) with the prose rules: all characters can climb, the non-thief moves at half rate, the dexterity Reaction/Attacking Adjustment applies, no special tools are assumed and the cracks and protuberances are assumed except on the gentle nonslippery slope, the encumbrance modifications (severe: the gentle nonslippery or slightly slippery slope at half; heavy or moderate: the gentle or moderate nonslippery or slightly slippery slope at half; light: any slope at full; the cliff face needs an unencumbered climber), the surface types (the gentle, moderate and severe degree bands and elevation changes, the cliff past 70 degrees, the overhang treated the same) and the chance of falling (100 minus the Climbing Rating; the non-thief 40 percent, the mountaineer with tools 80 percent on the restricted surfaces; the percentile roll at or under the rating succeeds) - the round opens the movement-across-special-terrain section. Census 359 -> 360.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed pp. 33-34; the user own copy OCR cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (every rate cell clean except the cliff smooth with-ledges row, where the djvu reads 16* for the non-slippery cell) and the IIIF full-resolution eye-reads (two eye-reads settle 15* - the 16* is an OCR artifact); every number matched.
banner.sentinel: The Table 15 movement figures are feet per round for a thief; every other character moves at half the indicated rate. The three rate columns are the non-slippery, slightly slippery and slippery conditions of the surface; the three flag columns carry the asterisk restriction. The chance of falling is 100 minus the Climbing Rating.

consts.name: wcsSurfaceCount
consts.comment: The Table 15 surface-row count (the nine slope rows and the four cliff rows).

consts.name: wcsSlopeRowBase
consts.comment: The slope rows begin at index 0 (the rough, normal and smooth surfaces at gentle, moderate and severe tilts).

consts.name: wcsCliffRowBase
consts.comment: The cliff rows begin at index 9 (rough and smooth, each with and without ledges).

consts.name: wcsGentleMinDeg
consts.comment: A gentle slope tilts at least 15 degrees.

consts.name: wcsGentleMaxDeg
consts.comment: A gentle slope tilts at most 30 degrees.

consts.name: wcsGentleRiseMin
consts.comment: The least extreme gentle slope rises 2 feet per 10 feet of horizontal distance.

consts.name: wcsGentleRiseMax
consts.comment: The most extreme gentle slope rises 5 feet per 10 feet of horizontal distance.

consts.name: wcsModerateMinDeg
consts.comment: A moderate slope tilts from 31 degrees.

consts.name: wcsModerateMaxDeg
consts.comment: A moderate slope tilts through 50 degrees.

consts.name: wcsModerateRiseMax
consts.comment: The most extreme moderate slope rises 12 feet per 10 feet of horizontal distance.

consts.name: wcsSevereMinDeg
consts.comment: A severe slope tilts from 51 degrees.

consts.name: wcsSevereMaxDeg
consts.comment: A severe slope tilts through 70 degrees.

consts.name: wcsSevereRiseMax
consts.comment: The most extreme severe slope rises 35 feet per 10 feet of horizontal distance.

consts.name: wcsCliffMinDeg
consts.comment: A cliff is any slope past 70 degrees.

consts.name: wcsHorizontalDist
consts.comment: The elevation changes are measured per 10 feet of horizontal distance on a line cutting through the slope.

consts.name: wcsNonThiefRating
consts.comment: The non-thief without mountaineering proficiency has a Climbing Rating of 40 percent.

consts.name: wcsMountaineerRating
consts.comment: The non-thief with mountaineering proficiency has a Climbing Rating of 80 percent when using his tools on a restricted surface.

consts.name: wcsFallBase
consts.comment: The chance of falling while climbing is 100 minus the Climbing Rating.

bools.name: wcsRateFeetPerRound
bools.comment: The Table 15 rates are expressed in feet per round for a thief.

bools.name: wcsAllCharactersCanClimb
bools.comment: All characters, not just thieves, have a chance to ascend, descend or move laterally across most non-horizontal natural surfaces.

bools.name: wcsNonThievesHalfRate
bools.comment: Every character other than a thief moves at one-half the indicated rate.

bools.name: wcsDexAdjustmentApplies
bools.comment: A character with exceptionally low or high dexterity applies his Reaction/Attacking Adjustment as a penalty or bonus to the climbing movement rate.

bools.name: wcsNoSpecialToolsAssumed
bools.comment: In all cases the climber is assumed to use no special tools other than a rope, which is of limited use for direct climbing unless used with other mountaineering equipment.

bools.name: wcsHandholdsAssumed
bools.comment: The surface is assumed to contain cracks or protuberances used as handholds and footholds.

bools.name: wcsGentleNonslipAidsOptional
bools.comment: On a gentle, nonslippery surface such aids are not necessary and do not have to be used even if present.

bools.name: wcsThievesOnlyDevoidSurfaces
bools.comment: Thieves are the only characters who can negotiate a surface completely devoid of handholds and footholds.

bools.name: wcsRestrictedThiefOrMountaineer
bools.comment: The asterisked Table 15 cells can be climbed only by a thief, or by a character with mountaineering proficiency who is using special tools.

bools.name: wcsSevereEncGentleOnlyHalf
bools.comment: A severely encumbered character can climb only a gentle nonslippery or slightly slippery slope, at one-half his normal climbing rate.

bools.name: wcsHeavyModerateEncGentleModerateHalf
bools.comment: A heavily or moderately encumbered character can climb only a gentle or moderate nonslippery or slightly slippery slope, at one-half his normal climbing rate.

bools.name: wcsLightEncAnySlopeFull
bools.comment: A lightly encumbered character can climb any slope (but not a cliff face) at his full normal climbing rate.

bools.name: wcsCliffRequiresUnencumbered
bools.comment: To climb a cliff face a thief or mountaineering-proficient character must be not encumbered - the gear carried must total less than the lower figure given for light encumbrance on the Encumbrance Limits for Characters Table.

bools.name: wcsUnderFifteenNotSlope
bools.comment: A tilt of less than 15 degrees is not a slope at all for these rules, and is moved across at the same speed as flat terrain.

bools.name: wcsOverhangSameRules
bools.comment: A cliff rising past 90 degrees is properly called an overhang, but it is not treated any differently.

bools.name: wcsFallIs100MinusRating
bools.comment: The chance of falling while climbing is a percentage equal to 100 minus the Climbing Rating.

bools.name: wcsThiefRatingIsClimbWalls
bools.comment: A thief Climbing Rating is the same as his climb walls score.

bools.name: wcsMountaineer80RestrictedOnly
bools.comment: The mountaineering 80 percent rating applies only when the tools are being used on a surface that only he (or a thief) is capable of climbing.

bools.name: wcsCheckRollUnderOrEqual
bools.comment: For each Climbing Check a percentile roll greater than the Climbing Rating fails, and a roll equal to or less than the Climbing Rating succeeds.

tables.name: Table 15: the climbing movement rates
col_comments: The non-slippery condition rate in feet per round for a thief by surface row (the rough, normal and smooth slopes at the gentle, moderate and severe tilts, then the cliff faces by roughness and ledges).
The slightly slippery condition rate in feet per round for a thief (0 = the same restricted meaning as the flags).
The slippery condition rate in feet per round for a thief.
The restricted flag for the non-slippery cell (1 = the asterisked cell: a thief or a mountaineering-proficient character with special tools only).
The restricted flag for the slightly slippery cell.
The restricted flag for the slippery cell.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 15 grid: the 13 surface rows (the rough, normal and smooth slopes at the gentle, moderate and severe tilts, then the cliff faces by roughness and ledges) x the three condition rates and the three restricted flags

examples.note: the rough gentle slope row: 90/60/30 feet per round - the fastest climb in the table, all three cells unrestricted
the normal slope severe row: only the slippery 5 cell is asterisked (a thief or a mountaineering-proficient character with tools)
the cliff rows: the rough with-ledges 25 is the best cliff rate, the smooth no-ledges row ends at 5, and every cliff cell is restricted
the unmodified non-thief falls 60 percent of the time (100 minus the 40 percent rating)
the degree bands: gentle 15 through 30, and the cliff begins past 70 degrees
